statement: A mortgage bond can secure repayment of a loan granted by a bank subsequent to its execution, including contingent liabilities, if it is a continuing security.
supporting_quote: A continuing security clause achieves this by providing that the mortgage shall remain a continuing security for the mortgagor’s obligations to the creditor at any time and that it shall not be satisfied or otherwise affected by any repayment from time to time of the whole or part of the sums due and owing,

statement: A co-owner of land who sues a trespasser for a declaration of title and ejectment is entitled to maintain the action even if he instituted the action as the sole owner of the land and premises.
supporting_quote: A co-owner of land who sues a trespasser for a declaration of title and ejectment is entitled to maintain the action even if he instituted the action as the sole owner of the land and premises. The fact that an appellant has asked for a greater relief than he is entitled to, should not prevent him from getting the lesser relief which he is entitled to. However, in such a situation, there is a burden on such person who makes the claim, to adduce evidence of ownership to the allotment of land.

statement: A transaction between a plaintiff and a defendant can be considered a nominal transfer if the plaintiff had only pledged their property to obtain a loan, and the court should consider attendant circumstances to determine the intention of the parties.
supporting_quote: Considering the attendant circumstances, I am of the view that the transaction was only a nominal transfer and the Plaintiff had only pledged her property to obtain a loan.

statement: A decision of the Land Commissioner cannot be arbitrary and unjustifiable.
supporting_quote: Thus, the said decision to abandon the move to give this land on a lease to the Petitioner-Appellant would be an arbitrary decision. The said decision is without justification.

statement: A co-owner of a land who sues a trespasser for a declaration of title and ejectment is entitled to maintain the action if he institutes the action as the sole owner of the premises.
supporting_quote: the fact that an appellant has asked for greater relief than he is entitled to should not prevent him from getting the lesser relief which he is entitled to

statement: A party invoking the provisions of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance to defeat the ownership of an adverse claimant to immovable property must establish a starting point for their acquisition of prescriptive rights.
supporting_quote: Where a party invokes the provisions of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance in order to defeat the ownership of an adverse claimant to immovable property, the burden of proof rests fairly and squarely on him to establish a starting point for his or her acquisition of prescriptive rights.

statement: The Petitioner Bank is entitled to execute the writ notwithstanding the notice of appeal, as Act No. 4 of 1990 has not provided for a right of appeal against an order made by the District Court in terms of Section 16 of the said Act.
supporting_quote: Act No. 4 of 1990 has not provided for a right of appeal against an order made by the District Court in terms of Section 16 of the said Act.

statement: The payment of stamp fees and the Notary's fees by the Plaintiff, taken together with the fact that the Plan No. 838 has been prepared just four days prior to the deed executed by the Defendant, is indicative of the fact that the Defendant had intended to part with his beneficial interest in the property to the Plaintiff.
supporting_quote: The payment of the stamp fees and the Notary’s fees by the Plaintiff, taken together with the fact that the Plan No. 838 has been prepared just four days prior to the deed executed by the Defendant, in our view, is not in favor of establishing a constructive trust as claimed by the Defendant, but indicative of the fact that the Defendant had intended to part with his beneficial interest in the property to the Plaintiff.

statement: The litis contestatio should be triggered at the point when the court is ready to frame issues based on the pleadings.
supporting_quote: Following the defendant's answer, the plaintiff may submit a replication as warranted by Section 79 of the CPC. Delivering interrogatories upon leave of court is also another optional step under Section 94(1) before the hearing, and it is in addition to the filing of a list of witnesses and documents within the stipulated period of time.

statement: A constructive trust arises where a person has transferred property subject to a notarial agreement to reconvey within a specified period, and they cannot enforce the agreement because the period has elapsed.
supporting_quote: If this is so, a trust under section 83 will also arise where a person has transferred property subject to a notarial agreement to reconvey within a specified period, and he cannot enforce the agreement because the period has elapsed.

statement: A document marked subject to proof is admissible without formal proof unless its execution or genuineness is impeached in the pleadings and raised as an issue, or the court otherwise requires proof.
supporting_quote: The law relating to the proof of documents has been laid down in the Civil Procedure Code (Amendment) Act, No. 17 of 2022. Section 2 of this Act introduces section 154A to be immediately inserted after section 154 of the principal enactment, which provides that when a deed or any document required by law to be attested is tendered in evidence, it shall be admissible without requiring formal proof, unless its execution or genuineness is impeached in the pleadings and raised as an issue, or the court otherwise requires proof.

statement: A bona fide purchaser's rights are unaffected by a constructive trust if the conditions of good faith and valuable consideration are established.
supporting_quote: However, upon reviewing the evidence, I am not satisfied that the conditions of good faith and valuable consideration have been established to the satisfaction of the Court.

statement: When deciding whether a prima facie case has been established by an applicant for an interim injunction, the court has to first satisfy itself that there is a serious question to be tried at the hearing and that on the facts and circumstances of each case whether there is a probability that the plaintiff is entitled to the relief claimed.
supporting_quote: When deciding whether a prima facie case has been established by an applicant for an interim injunction, the court has to first satisfy itself that there is a serious question to be tried at the hearing and that on the facts and circumstances of each case whether there is a probability that the plaintiff is entitled to the relief claimed.

statement: A person who possesses a land with a secret intention that he would be able to claim prescription at the end of ten years is not entitled to claim prescription under Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: If a person, who claims prescription in terms of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance, possesses the property with a secret intention his possession cannot be considered as an adverse possession and as such he is not entitled to succeed in a claim of prescription.

statement: A wider and purposive construction must be preferred to a narrow and restrictive approach when determining an application for the addition of parties under section 18(1) of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: In determining an application for the addition of parties under section 18(1) of the Civil Procedure Code, a wider and purposive construction must be preferred to a narrow and restrictive approach.

statement: A transferee holds a property in trust for the transferor if the transferor did not intend to dispose of the beneficial interest, as inferred from attendant circumstances.
supporting_quote: When the attendant circumstances show that the transferor did not intend to dispose the beneficial interest of the property to the transferee, then the law declares that the transferee would hold such property for the benefit of the transferor.

statement: A wife cannot claim prescriptive title to a property owned by her husband, as her possession of the property is not considered adverse possession.
supporting_quote: Further when wife possesses a property of her husband she cannot claim prescriptive title under Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance against her husband because such a possession cannot be considered to be an adverse possession against her husband.

statement: The mere fact that Dingiri Banda is identified as a close relative of Siyathuhamy is insufficient by itself to make the information about his mother relevant in terms of section 32(5) of the Evidence Ordinance in view of the contradictory nature of the evidence before court on this issue.
supporting_quote: Therefore, I hold that the details of the mother of Siyathuhamy set out in the death certificate (4D4) are not relevant in terms of section 32(5) of the Evidence Ordinance.

statement: Courts do not act on the principle that every procedure is prohibited unless it is expressly provided by the law, but on the converse principle that every procedure is permissible till it is shown to be prohibited by the law.
supporting_quote: It must be stated here that what is expressly stated excludes the others. As shown above, there are express provisions in the Civil Procedure Code which provides for the addition of parties and intervention in an action.

statement: Lots B and C of the Preliminary Plan cannot be excluded from the land to be partitioned.
supporting_quote: I hold that Lots B and C of the Preliminary Plan cannot be excluded from the land to be partitioned.

statement: A party who did not file the list of witnesses and documents as required by section 79B can invoke section 142D to call additional witnesses and produce additional documents at the pre-trial conference, but only if the other party consents to it.
supporting_quote: A party who did not file the list as required by section 79B cannot invoke this provision unless the other party consents to it at the pre-trial conference.

statement: A person cannot transfer what they do not have.
supporting_quote: He cannot transfer what he does not have.

statement: A party to an action cannot lead evidence of rebuttal in an instance where the defendant was ordered to begin, as it would be a case materially different from that which he has placed on record.
supporting_quote: Evidence must reasonably accord with party's pleadings and no party can set up at trial a case which is materially different from that which he has placed on record

statement: A party claiming prescription must establish an overt act of ouster.
supporting_quote: Other than making bare claims that “I was in possession” and “I tapped rubber” the 2nd to 6th Defendants failed to present any evidence of ouster.

statement: A judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction operates as an estoppel under the principle of estoppel per rem judicatam.
supporting_quote: where a final judicial decision has been pronounced by either an English, (or with certain exemptions) a foreign judicial tribunal of competent jurisdiction over the parties to, and the subject matter of, the litigation, any party or privy to such litigation, as against any other party or privy thereto, and, in the case of a decision in rem, any person whatsoever, as against any other person, is estopped in any subsequent litigation from disputing or questioning such decision on the merits, whether it be used as the foundation of an action, or relied upon as a bar to a claim, indictment or complaint, or to any affirmative defence, case, or allegation, if, but not unless, the party interested raises the point of estoppel at the proper time and in the proper manner.
